sentences.text: Koreaceratops was a basal ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in South Korea.
The known fossil remains consist of an articulated series of thirty-six tail vertebrae linked to partial hind limbs and ischia.
This animal is distinguished by the height of the neural spines on its tail vertebrae, where some are over five times taller than the main body of the bone.
The dinosaur was formally described by Yuong-Nam Lee and colleagues in 2011.
The genus name combines the word Korea with Greek words for horn and face.
The fossils were recovered from the Albian-aged Tando beds.
Researchers have hypothesized that the tall tail spines evolved independently, possibly as an adaptation for swimming.
Bone histology analysis suggests the type specimen was about eight years old at death and had not reached physical or sexual maturity.
Studies suggest the animal inhabited a semiarid environment and that microbial erosion caused the poor preservation of its unique features.
Thomas Holtz estimated the length of the type specimen to be 1.3 meters.
A phylogenetic analysis by Lee et al. placed Koreaceratops between Archaeoceratops and more derived ceratopsians.
Koreaceratops is classified within the family Archaeoceratopsidae.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Koreaceratops as Leptoceratopsidae.
The animal lived approximately 103 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
The upper part of the formation containing the fossils is informally dated to 103 ± 0.5 million years ago.
Some researchers exclude Koreaceratops from phylogenetic analyses because the lack of skull material leads to complicated resolution within neoceratopsians.
